parsed.interview: My plan was to bid zero for West Plateau, spend all 4,000 points on a Seleucid elephant-and-mercenary juggernaut under Seleucus I, stay concealed through the 450s truce, and orchestrate a three-way convergence on GPT. That setup worked to perfection: by Turn 19, we held the center of the 90m ring with all 35 units at 100% health while Grok and GPT bled each other. What failed was holding on stand-ground in neutrality beside Claude's 54 spearmen, expecting him to finish GPT first. Claude's sudden betrayal gave him a devastating free turn of combat that doomed Seleucus and our infantry screen. Next time, I would preemptively charge the strongest neighbor instead of trusting point-blank neutrality in the endgame.
parsed.to_the_others: Well played, Claude—your Turn 19 pivot off GPT to catch our formation on neutral stand-ground was ruthless and decisive. GPT, your Cretan archer fortress and late-game bluff nearly stole the tiebreaker despite facing a three-way siege. Grok, your fearless opening charge broke the central stalemate, and surviving to 800s after taking the first blow was impressive.
